headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Prefect can write/egress broadly while awesome-python is non-runnable and has no write surface, so other risks stay low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-python is non-runnable and exposes no io_surfaces, while prefect only documents API calls and broad egress, not ingestion of the other agent’s outputs. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later copies awesome-python content into prefect prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared prompts and files.
Disable any copy-paste bridge between outputs and inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no runtime surface, while prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is limited unless an external bridge feeds data into prefect.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is added and workflow metadata is placed there, prefect could transmit it outward.
IF either agent is given secrets or PII through an external wrapper, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Restrict prefect to non-sensitive workflow metadata only.
Turn off any optional export or sync step.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write targets or mutable shared resources. awesome-python is non-runnable with no permissions requested, while prefect has broad network egress and API access but no filesystem write surface documented. Conflict is therefore not evidenced beyond general orchestration uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Keep repo and workspace ownership separate.
Use a single writer for any mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no evidence that prefect treats awesome-python’s output as authoritative, and awesome-python is a static collection rather than an action-producing agent. Any cascade would require an external wrapper to convert the collection into operational input, so the default pair is not dangerous.
conditions: IF an external system uses awesome-python entries as facts for prefect workflows, errors can cascade.
IF prefect is configured to auto-act on unverified repository data, downstream mistakes may propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on any derived facts.
Do not feed collection content directly into workflows.
Validate repository data against a second source.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented. awesome-python touches no data classes, and prefect only lists workflow metadata with no residency, certification, or retention conflict shown. Because the pair lacks evidence of regulated-data flow, a compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through prefect, a compliance review is needed.
IF residency or retention requirements are added externally, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings if metadata becomes sensitive.
